candidates.description: A strong positive patch test reaction creates an 'angry back' which becomes hyper-reactive to other patch test challenges
candidates.citation_sentence: The term 'jingry back syndrome' (ABS) was coined by Mitchell in 197S.
candidates.notes: The paper explicitly concludes ABS is a non-reproducible phenomenon; all experiments failed to demonstrate the angry back effect. The paper explicitly states it failed to reproduce ABS in any group tested (nickel-sensitive subjects, normal controls, and subjects with prior ABS history). The original Mitchell (1975) study reportedly contained no supporting data; this replication attempted to test the phenomenon using patch-testing methodology with dose-response thresholds. No DOI for Mitchell (1975) is provided in the paper, so original_url is left blank.

candidates.original_title: The angry back syndrome: eczema creates angry eczema
candidates.description: A strong positive patch-test reaction creates an 'angry back' state in which the skin becomes generally or locally hyperreactive to other patch-test challenges and produces multiple concomitant positive reactions.
candidates.citation_sentence: The term  'jingry  back  syndrome' (ABS) was coined by Mitchell  in  197S.
candidates.notes: The paper tested generalized hyperreactivity, localized hyperreactivity, individual-specificity, and reproducibility of the angry back syndrome and concluded that the phenomenon could not be reproduced.
